readout_other: Optical-resolution photoacoustic microscopy (PA intensity, vessel area fraction, vessel diameter, branch points, perfused vessel density); TTC infarct staining
direction_notes: LITUS after photothrombotic stroke restored PA signal intensity, perfused vessel density and vessel diameter toward baseline and reduced infarct area at 24 h versus untreated PT mice.
safety_notes: Cortical temperature elevation below 2 C; mechanical index calculated as 1.16.

exposures.label: LITUS of photothrombotic lesion, left cortex

target.label: cortical target coordinates (AP = -2.0 mm, ML = -2.0 mm)

timing.protocol_description: PRF 1 kHz, duty cycle 20%, sonication duration 300 ms; total treatment duration 10 min starting 23 min after the photothrombotic procedure.

source_quotes.n_subjects: In the therapeutic evaluation cohort, animals were assigned to three groups: No-PT control, PT without intervention, and PT followed by LITUS treatment, with five animals per group.
source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: The TUS system consisted of a single-element focused ultrasound transducer (Siansonic, AQ20- 1020) operating at a center frequency of 1 MHz, with a focal length of 20 mm, a focal width of 2 mm, and an axial focal length of 12 mm.
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.pulse_repetition_fre: The system operated at a pulse repetition frequency of 1 kHz, a duty cycle of 20%, and a sonication duration of 300 ms.

source_quotes.exposures[0].unspecified_domain.ispta_w_: The total treatment duration was 10 min, and the spatial peak temporal average intensity $\left( \mathrm { { I } _ { \mathrm { { S P T A } } } } \right)$ was 450 mW/cm<sup>2</sup>. Based on the measured peak negative pressure of 1.16 MPa, the corresponding Mechanical Index (MI) was calculated to be 1.16. Local temperature-rise testing further showed that the cortical temperature elevation under the present stimulation conditions remained below $2 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C } ,$ , supporting that the exposure was delivered within a low-risk acoustic and thermal window.
